questions.explanation: An it-cleft focuses the subject: 'It was the treasurer who' emphasises who, not what.
questions.q: It was the treasurer ___ signed the cheque, not the chair.

questions.explanation: Extraposition moves a long subject clause to the end, with 'it' as the dummy subject.
questions.q: ___ is clear that the figures were manipulated.

questions.explanation: In the cleft, 'when' pairs with the time focus; 'that' would shift the focus to place.
questions.q: It was in the vault ___ the alarm was triggered. (focus on time)

questions.explanation: The cleft 'It was only after' focuses the timing, with the rest in a that-clause.
questions.q: It was only after the audit ___ the truth came out.

questions.explanation: Extraposition with 'it' + adjective + to-infinitive is the natural evaluative pattern.
questions.q: It is unwise ___ sign without reading the contract.

questions.explanation: The cleft focuses the cause with 'that' introducing the focused subject.
questions.q: It was the storm ___ delayed the shipment. (focus on cause)

questions.explanation: The cleft focuses 'last year'; the pronoun must introduce the time clause.
questions.q: It was last year ___ she joined the firm.

questions.explanation: Extraposed 'it' with a that-clause reports the belief naturally; the subject-clause version is clumsy.
questions.q: It is thought ___ he lied to the committee.

questions.explanation: In an it-cleft the relative agrees with the focused noun: 'the basement where', not 'when'.
questions.q: It was the basement ___ they found the documents. (focus on place)

questions.explanation: Extraposition of a long infinitive subject uses dummy 'it': 'It takes courage to...'.
questions.q: It takes courage ___ speak out.

questions.explanation: 'It was not until' is the standard cleft for focusing a late time point.
questions.q: It was not until midnight ___ the guests left.

questions.explanation: Extraposition with adjectives of importance uses 'it is vital that' + subjunctive base form.
questions.q: It is vital that he ___ informed immediately.

questions.explanation: The extraposed 'it is possible that' hedges the claim while keeping the clause at the end.
questions.q: It is possible ___ the train will be late.

questions.explanation: The cleft focuses the instrument with 'with' + 'that'; 'where' cannot introduce the means.
questions.q: It was with a crowbar ___ they forced the door. (focus on instrument)

questions.explanation: Only the it-cleft puts the stress on the final chapter; the others stress different elements.
options: The final chapter revealed the killer.
It was the final chapter that revealed the killer.
The killer was revealed by the final chapter.
What revealed the killer was the final chapter.
questions.q: Choose the sentence that emphasises THE FINAL CHAPTER.

questions.explanation: 'It is no use' + gerund is the idiomatic extraposed form; the subject-gerund version is unnatural.
options: Crying over spilt milk it is no use.
It no use is crying over spilt milk.
It is no use crying over spilt milk.
No use it is to cry over spilt milk.
questions.q: Which version is the natural extraposed form?

questions.explanation: The cleft focuses the instrument with the prepositional phrase intact.
options: It was a crowbar which they forced the door.
It was a crowbar where they forced the door.
It was with a crowbar that they forced the door.
It was with a crowbar where they forced the door.
questions.q: Select the correct it-cleft emphasising the instrument.

questions.explanation: Extraposed 'it seems that' is natural; the bare subject-clause version is awkward.
questions.q: Choose the natural extraposed sentence.

questions.explanation: The cleft 'It is the results that matter' focuses the subject against the alternative.
options: The results matter, not the intentions.
It are the results who matter, not the intentions.
The results are that matter, not the intentions.
It is the results that matter, not the intentions.
questions.q: Which sentence correctly emphasises the results?

questions.explanation: Extraposed 'it' + adjective + that-clause evaluates the situation; the long subject version is unnatural.
options: That he should confess surprises no one.
Surprising it is that he should confess.
It surprises no one that he should confess.
It no one surprises that he confessed.
questions.q: Pick the natural extraposed version.
